Hi Rachel —

Attached is a draft addendum and the order form that reflects the seat ramp you outlined on last week's call (50 seats in Q1 -> 250 by month 9). Key points we tried to capture:
- Shift to a 12-month term aligned to the renewal window
- Step-down pricing for incremental seats beyond 300
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing with a 30-day payment term

Karthik and Ben are cc'd for legal/ops sanity checks. Please review and flag any hard stops from procurement or legal on your side. If the ramp schedule needs to be accelerated we can surface a burst capacity add-on in the SOW.

Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2029 11:08:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft addendum + ramp schedule (seed for redlines)

Naomi —

Thanks for the draft. We like the direction but have a few redlines from procurement and legal. High level:
1) Term: Procurement prefers staying on a 24-month minimum for this commit size; our legal will accept 12 months only with a limited early termination liability cap.
2) Audit & data retention: we need a clearer audit clause and a 7-year data retention carveout for logs related to security investigations.
3) SLA credits: want explicit financial credits for consecutive days of degraded availability (our SRE team escalates this).

I've looped Monica from procurement; she'll coordinate PO timing and internal approval. We'll return a redline by Thursday EOD.

Rachel Wu
Director, Cloud Platform Partnerships
AcmeCloud
rachel.wu@acmecloud.com

Thanks Rachel —

Appreciate the transparency. To keep momentum, we're fine to accept the 12-month term if AcmeCloud will commit to the ramp schedule and the seat milestones trigger the step-down pricing as proposed. On the audit/data retention items, can we limit audit frequency to annually and require 30 days' notice? That has been the standard compromise for similar accounts.

I've attached a lightly redlined order form that accepts the term shift but keeps audit limits and invoice cadence consistent (see ACME_OrderForm-v3-redline.docx). If procurement needs a longer term for internal approvals, happy to discuss a short side letter that documents expected ramp dates and pricing.

- Ben

Date: Wed, 31 Jul 2029 14:20:05 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft addendum + ramp schedule (seed for redlines)

Naomi / team —

Reading Rachel's note and Ben's redline. A few legal points we should propose to AcmeCloud as compromise language:
- Term: Accept 12 months if an early-termination liability is capped at the lesser of 3 months' remaining fees or the committed ramp value at signature.
- Audit: Annual audit rights with no more than one (1) full-scope audit per 12 months; Redwood will require 30 days' notice and an agreed scope.
- Data retention carveouts: We can accept retention for security logs up to 7 years but require controls around access and a mutually agreeable redaction process.
- SLA credits: Offer up to 10% credit for monthly unavailability below contracted SLA, escalating per consecutive days; exclude scheduled maintenance and customer-caused outages.

I'll prepare a suggested clause file (attached) and highlight the lines to propose in-track so procurement can decide. If they insist on 24 months, we should ask for an uplift in the committed seat counts/pricing or a signing credit.

Attachment: MSA_addendum_clause_suggested.txt

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 1 Aug 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Draft addendum + ramp schedule (seed for redlines)

Rachel / Monica —

Great progress — thank you. Next steps and our positions below so procurement/legal have a clear path: 
1) Term: Redwood will accept the 12-month term provided AcmeCloud agrees to the early-termination liability cap Karthik proposed. We'll include the cap as a fallback in the addendum.
2) Ramp schedule: Redwood requires the seat milestone commitments (50 -> 250 by month 9) in the SOW; if Acme needs faster capacity we can add a temporary burst line item billed separately.
3) Audit & retention: Annual audit only, 30 days' notice, restricted scope. We accept a security-log retention carveout to 7 years with redaction controls and access logs.
4) SLA credits: accept limited financial credits per the suggested schedule; exclude scheduled maintenance and customer-caused impacts.

If that framework is acceptable, please return a single redlined order form and we'll prepare the final addendum + DocuSign package. I've created a DocuSign record to speed execution: https://redwoodapp.docusign.com/ACME-2029-RNW-42.

Attachments to finalize: ACME_OrderForm-v3-redline.docx, SOW_seat-ramp_schedule.xlsx

Would you like us to produce a short side letter for procurement to speed internal approvals while legal finishes the MSA addendum language? Happy to draft.

Thanks —
